title: WebSocket Protocol
body:
A protocol giving a **persistent, two-way** connection between browser and server, which
[[HTTP]] cannot do. This is the "push architecture" listed among [[Node.js]]'s advantages.

The problem it solves: HTTP is request/response and the [[Client]] always speaks first, so a
server with new information has no way to say so. The workarounds are polling (ask every few
seconds, mostly getting "nothing new") and long polling (hold the request open until there is
something), both of which waste requests and add latency.

A WebSocket starts life as an HTTP request carrying `Upgrade: websocket`. If the server
agrees, the same TCP connection stops speaking HTTP and becomes a bidirectional message
channel that stays open. After that either side can send at any time, with no request needed.

```js
const socket = new WebSocket("wss://example.com/feed");
socket.addEventListener("message", (e) => console.log(e.data));
socket.send("hello");
```

Chat, live dashboards, multiplayer, collaborative editing, and anything with a price ticker.
The cost is that the connection is stateful and long-lived, which is exactly the property
[[Stateless Protocol|statelessness]] gave up in order to scale, so a WebSocket server holds
one open connection per user and a [[Load Balancer]] in front of it has to keep sending that
user to the same machine.

`wss://` is the TLS version, same relationship as [[HTTPS]] to HTTP.
